RUSSL CORPUS 2.0.0 · SCOPED PIXEL ADAPTER
One field. Every pixel addressed.
4 × 4 × 4 × 16 × 16 scalar sites, stored in a 128 × 128 Float64 TIFF atlas. Capture and edit a staged image; only Apply changes the live XPU.




Refresh to inspect the staged TIFF.


Inspect or edit a scalar site
c4 selects real (0), imaginary (1), intensity (2), or phase (3). c5/c6 select a 16 × 16 tile; c7/c8 select its row/column. Intensity and phase are read-only derivatives.


No site selected.
Edits round explicitly to the existing XPU's Float32 precision and report the effective value. Intensity and phase are recalculated together. Your live XPU stays unchanged until Apply.


Field record
No staged TIFF loaded.


Sample-exact versus visual exports
The atlas stores real and imaginary Float32 samples widened exactly into Float64 slots, plus derived intensity and phase. No pixels are padding. Ordinary phase.tif remains a quantized unsigned 16-bit visualization and now declares that loss in its metadata.
Applying an atlas resets the GIF spool, recordings, byte lanes, counters and derived caches. Export a full volume backup before replacing a session you need to retain.


Format and execution boundary
Bounded, finite grayscale TIFF: little/big endian, classic TIFF or small BigTIFF, uncompressed strips. Atlas imports require the exact declared placement profile and matching sample checksum. Unsupported metadata, compression or page stacking is rejected.
The corpus's language, mechanics and OME-Zarr proposals remain separate. This adapter does not execute metadata or turn TIFF pixels into independent silicon, optical hardware, or a complete RUSSL/MSSL runtime.


RAM-RESIDENT PHASE AND NEURON PIPELINE
Semi-sili XPU
Sample the live field, evolve a finite p-adic neuron bank, then read its numerical phase. GPU-required runs confirm every arithmetic result through WebGPU before Save is enabled.


Run a checked preview










The modulus prime raised to precision must be at most 65,536. The operand must be smaller than that modulus. Negation and digit complement are separate operations.

Sampled preview
The CPU models wave phases and finite neuron evolution. GPU confirmation covers exact ring arithmetic. Saving publishes the checked Float32 field and its neuron bank together.
Neuron amplitude is a numerical coupling. Quantum, optical and physical in-DRAM operations are research models; this pipeline uses the laptop's existing CPU and available GPU.


Keep and inspect a result
Each logical cell has five exact 32-bit words: residue, activation, amplitude, real field and imaginary field. A TIFF byte raster retains those 20 bytes; the five logical coordinate axes are declared in its metadata.
Up to eight prior frames are retained in the saved bank. TIFF carries one frame. Imported files are checked before Save; their old GPU status is never treated as a fresh measurement. Export a full volume backup from Virtual storage.

EXECUTION BOUNDARY
What this build actually does.
Console → worker → storage
The compiled native presenter opens this browser application through WebView2. The optional WebSocket launcher connects HERMIT terminals to the same XPU worker through localhost. XPU terminals share one numerical engine and virtual volume. Administrator PowerShell is a separate Windows terminal, opened explicitly through Windows elevation; Invoke-JA21Terminal sends work to XPU 1 or 2 and returns its completed result.
The SPIRAL shell has quoting, variables, aliases, pipelines, redirects, history, and a bounded virtual filesystem. It is not Bash, PowerShell, or a host operating system.
CPU models and measured GPU confirmation
The field simulator computes Fourier propagation, optical gate models, phase retrieval, GIF spooling, and LUT transformations in JavaScript. Legacy “GPU” byte loops remain batched CPU loops. The Semi-sili XPU tab dispatches a separate WebGPU integer kernel and records actual readback confirmation when available.
Landauer-related values are transition-cost proxies, not measured heat. Bloch, Wigner, and penteract values are model-derived visualizations, not measurements of quantum hardware or physical five-dimensional storage.
Data protection
A single-writer Web Lock and transactional revision checks prevent cooperating windows from overwriting one another. Recovery validates snapshots before replacing live state. Corrupt data never triggers a factory reset.
Checksums detect accidental changes; they are not signatures or authentication. Keep exported backups. Old releases do not honor the new lock protocol and should not run on the same origin.
Release 2.4.0
Open the browser validation kit. It uses an isolated test volume and exports CPU, GPU and persistence results.
No third-party runtime package installation. Original research attachments remain unchanged under references/. The removed cloud/auth scaffold and original generated outputs are retained in audit/legacy-scaffold.zip, not served by the app.
See AUDIT_REPORT.md, CHANGELOG.md, and the reproducible test suite in the release folder. The native console requires WebView2 and uses the existing CPU/GPU. The optional developer launcher provisions a hash-verified private Node.js runtime.
